newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasolines up after PADD 5 gas draw.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasolines up after PADD 5 gas draw.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices jumped late Tueday after a weekly oil inventory report showed the region's gasoline supply continued its steep springtime decline, traders said.
West Coast gasoline stocks fell 1.3 million barrels last week to 28.3 million, according to a weekly inventory report released Tuesday by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
The decline added to a recent drop-off in stocks that leaves PADD 5 West Coast refiners scrambling to buy supply amid a heavy shutdown period for spring maintenance.
"We've had a two million-barrel draw in three weeks. That's why everyone's spooked," one broker said.

In West Coast spot trade, a March cargo of CARB gasoline sold at 75 cents in L.A., with an April deal inked at 71 cents. March grade was talked between 75.50 to 76 cents late Tuesday, 2.50 to three cents over Monday levels.
Later deliveries of product remained cheaper on expectations refiners would resume production after spring maintenance.
L.A. conventional unleaded gasoline traded at 69.75 cents, and was talked late at 71/72 cents, an increase of three cents from late yesterday.
Distillates in northern and southern California were narrowly mixed in late trade.
San Francisco products shrugged off news of a presumed leak on Santa Fe Pacific Pipeline, which forced operators to shut part of the line between Sacramento and Reno, Nevada.
A state official said investigators are digging through snow to determine why diesel fuel might be leaking from the line.
Meanwhile, Bay area refiners have been advised to truck refined product to Reno.
Most trucks will pick up conventional gasoline in Chico, California and drive it to Reno, said a trader for a large refiner in San Francisco.
A segment to Chico, a terminal north of Sacramento, remains open and the trader said trucking rates from there to Reno are cheaper than from Sacramento.
"They'll move as much conventional gasoline out of Chico," as possible, he said. "The trucking rate is cheaper."
